newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq stocks hit new record, techs firm.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq stocks hit new record, techs firm.

text.p: Nasdaq shares rallied to their second consecutive record high on Thursday, riding on the strength of technology shares and broad market gains after a tame jobs report, traders said.

In a shortened session ahead of the Independence Day holiday weekend, the Nasdaq composite index gained 12 points or 0.82 percent to close unofficially at 1467.61, topping the previous record of 1455.62 set on Wednesday. Advancing issues beat decliners 2164 to 1732 on slim volume of 374 million shares.

"It was a short day. There's really nothing else to do but buy after the employment report and the Fed keeping rates steady yesterday," said one trader. The employement report released Thursday morning pointed to modest growth in wages and new jobs, sparking a broad rally in stocks and bonds.
Several key technology stocks also added to gains seen Wednesday, with Dell Computer Corp, Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp gaining ground.
INSO Corp, the most active Nasdaq issue, dropped almost 47 percent after it said expects its second quarter earnings will fall significantly below Wall Street estimates.
